title: Baklava: Walnut and Pistachio Pastry Squares in Honey Syrup
summary: Buttered filo layered with a coarse walnut and pistachio filling, cut into squares, baked golden and drenched with a cold honey and lemon syrup.

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.text: Put the sugar, honey and water in the small pan and bring to a gentle boil, stirring until the sugar has dissolved. Add the lemon peel and simmer for 15 min until the syrup lightly coats a spoon. Remove the peel, stir in the orange blossom water if using, then cool and chill for at least 1 h. Cold syrup on hot pastry is what keeps baklava crisp.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Pulse the pistachios and walnuts in the food processor in two batches until coarsely ground with some pea-size pieces left; do not let it turn to paste. Mix with the sugar and cinnamon.

steps.title: Prepare the pastry
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175 °C (155 °C fan). Trim the filo stack to the size of the dish if needed and keep it covered with the damp towel while you work, as it dries out within minutes.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Brush the dish with melted butter. Lay in 2 sheets, brush the top sheet with butter, and keep going in buttered pairs until about a third of the filo is used.

steps.title: Layer the nuts
steps.text: Scatter half the nut mixture evenly over the base. Cover with 3 buttered pairs of sheets, then spread the remaining nuts and press lightly. Use the rest of the filo in buttered pairs for the top and brush it generously.

steps.title: Cut before baking
steps.text: With the serrated knife cut right down to the base in 6 rows by 4 to make 24 squares. Cutting now gives clean pieces and lets the syrup reach every layer.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 40-50 min, turning the dish halfway, until deep golden across the top and edges. Check from 40 min; pale baklava turns soggy once soaked.

steps.title: Soak and rest
steps.text: Straight from the oven, spoon the cold syrup evenly over the hot pastry, making sure the corners and edges get their share; it will sizzle. Leave uncovered at room temperature for at least 6 h before lifting out the squares.

tips: Keep the filo under a damp, not wet, towel; wet patches make the sheets stick together.
Torn sheets are fine in the middle layers; save the best ones for the top.
Do not cover the baklava while it soaks, or condensation will soften the top.
storage: Keep loosely covered at room temperature for up to 5 days. Do not refrigerate, as the pastry turns chewy. Freezes well for up to 3 months.
